name: Eliminating the components of null order yields a homomorphic image
description: Exercise 4.66: if Z@ = RSY(SCR), M = {Z$ : Z$ in VSCR; Z$ is not of null order for SCR} = {Zi1,...,Zim}, VSCR$ = (Zi1,...,Zim) and CSCR$ = {(B, A) in CSCR : the ports belong to components of VSCR$}, then Z@$ = RSY(SCR$) and Z@$ = HIMSY(Z@, PJN({SZ$ : Z$ in VSCR$}), ID(IZ@), ID(OZ@)).

elements.text: M = {Z$ : Z$ in VSCR; Z$ is not of null order for SCR}, enumerated as Zi1,...,Zim with distinct indices i1,...,im in IJS[1, n].
VSCR$ = (Zi1,...,Zim) is a subvector of VSCR.
CSCR$ = {(B, A) : (B, A) in CSCR; there exists Z$ in VSCR$ such that the port belongs to Z$}.
A component coupled to a component of some order is itself of some order, so no connection of CSCR joins a deleted component to a retained one.
IZ@$ = IZ@: every unconnected input port of SCR belongs to a component of order 0, hence is retained, and stays unconnected in SCR$.
OZ@$ = OZ@: every unconnected output port of SCR belongs to a component of order 0, hence is retained, and stays unconnected in SCR$.
HS = PJN({SZ$ : Z$ in VSCR$}), the projection of the resultant state onto the retained components.
Z@$ = HIMSY(Z@, PJN({SZ$ : Z$ in VSCR$}), ID(IZ@), ID(OZ@)).
There exists Z@$ in DSYSTEMS with Z@$ = RSY(SCR$) and Z@$ = HIMSY(Z@, PJN({SZ$ : Z$ in VSCR$}), ID(IZ@), ID(OZ@)).
